desc:
You are given an arbitrary binary tree (it may not be a BST). A subtree is a node together with all of its descendants. A subtree is a valid BST when for every node inside it all values in the left part are strictly smaller and all values in the right part strictly larger than that node (so duplicates make it invalid). A single node is always a valid BST.

Return the largest number of nodes in a subtree that is a valid BST. The empty tree gives 0.

Tree encoding. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level order. The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn, level by level, from left to right. A missing child is written as -1 (node values are never negative, so -1 cannot be confused with a value). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped. The empty tree is [].

For example, [8,3,10,1,6,-1,14] is the tree whose root 8 has children 3 and 10; node 3 has children 1 and 6; node 10 has no left child and right child 14.

Example 1

tree = [10,5,15,1,8,-1,7]
Output: 3
The whole tree is not a BST (7 is in the right subtree of 15 but smaller). The subtree rooted at 5 with children 1 and 8 is a BST of 3 nodes.

Example 2

tree = [2,1,3]
Output: 3

Example 3

tree = [4,4,4]
Output: 1
Equal values break the strict order, so only single nodes qualify.
hints: Testing every node separately by running a full BST validation on its subtree works, but it is O(n * h) or worse. Can each subtree reuse what its children already know?
A node roots a valid BST exactly when its left subtree is a valid BST whose maximum is below the node, and its right subtree is a valid BST whose minimum is above the node.
Process nodes bottom-up (in reverse level order). For each node store whether its subtree is a valid BST and, if so, its size, minimum and maximum. Keep the largest size of any valid one.
editorial: Work bottom-up, so that every node can use the summary of its two children. For a valid BST subtree we store three numbers: its size, its smallest value and its largest value. A node with left summary L and right summary R forms a valid BST when each present child is itself valid, L.max < value and R.min > value. Its size is L.size + R.size + 1, its minimum is L.min (or its own value if there is no left child) and its maximum is R.max (or its own value). Otherwise the node is marked invalid, and so are all its ancestors, since a subtree containing an invalid part cannot be a BST.

Decoding the array yields nodes in level order, where children always come after their parent; iterating the indices in reverse is therefore a valid bottom-up order and needs no recursion. Time O(n), space O(n).
solution:
def parse(tree):
    val, left, right = [tree[0]], [-1], [-1]
    i, u = 1, 0
    while u < len(val) and i < len(tree):
        for kids in (left, right):
            if i < len(tree):
                x = tree[i]
                i += 1
                if x != -1:
                    kids[u] = len(val)
                    val.append(x)
                    left.append(-1)
                    right.append(-1)
        u += 1
    return val, left, right


def largestBstSubtree(tree):
    if not tree:
        return 0
    val, left, right = parse(tree)
    n = len(val)
    ok = [False] * n
    size = [0] * n
    lo = [0] * n
    hi = [0] * n
    best = 0
    for u in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        l, r = left[u], right[u]
        if (l == -1 or (ok[l] and hi[l] < val[u])) and (r == -1 or (ok[r] and lo[r] > val[u])):
            ok[u] = True
            size[u] = 1 + (size[l] if l != -1 else 0) + (size[r] if r != -1 else 0)
            lo[u] = lo[l] if l != -1 else val[u]
            hi[u] = hi[r] if r != -1 else val[u]
            if size[u] > best:
                best = size[u]
    return best
